subtitle: How a Tang Envoy Rode the Storm After Harsha’s Fall

panels.shot: epic wide shot, low angle, showing Wang Xuance on horseback at a mountain pass between snow peaks and the plains, half in shadow, half in light
panels.action: Wang Xuance sits alert on a sturdy horse at a high Himalayan pass, Tibetans and Nepalese soldiers behind him, the misty plains of the Ganga valley stretching far below.

dialogue.text: When Emperor Harsha died heirless, a Chinese envoy named Wang Xuance rode into a power vacuum—and returned with a borrowed army to settle a usurper’s gamble.

i18n.hi: जब सम्राट हर्ष बिना वारिस के मरे, तो वांग श्वान्से नाम का चीनी दूत उस सत्ता शून्य में घुसा—और गद्दार की बाज़ी चुकाने उधारी सेना लेकर लौटा।

panels.shot: broad aerial view over the Ganga plain, with Kannauj glimmering on the riverbank
panels.action: The camera glides above the wide Ganga plain, fields and towns dotting the river’s curve, with the fortified city of Kannauj rising on a bend like a crown of stone and brick.

dialogue.text: For decades, Kannauj under Harsha stood as a great court of northern India, its riverfront palaces drawing monks, merchants, and envoys from lands as far as the Tang empire.

i18n.hi: दशकों तक हर्ष के अधीन कन्नौज उत्तर भारत का महान दरबार रहा, नदी किनारे के महल जहाँ दूर तांग साम्राज्य से भी भिक्षु, व्यापारी और दूत उमड़ते थे।

panels.shot: intimate interior wide of Harsha’s empty court hall, shafts of dust-filled light
panels.action: An ornate throne hall with carved pillars and empty seats lies still in motes of dust and light, garlands wilted, drums silent, a royal umbrella folded on the floor.

dialogue.text: Then, around 647, the chronicles say, Harsha died without an heir. His court fell silent, and the question everyone feared hung in the air—who now ruled Kannauj?

i18n.hi: फिर, लगभग 647 में, लिखा है कि हर्ष बिना उतराधिकारी के मर गए। दरबार सुनसान पड़ा, और डरती हुई फुसफुसाहट हवा में थी—अब कन्नौज का मालिक कौन?

panels.shot: shadowed medium shot of a figure seizing a throne, seen from behind to keep him generic
panels.action: From behind, a broad-shouldered figure in royal ornaments strides up the steps of the vacant throne and sits with sudden authority as a few wary courtiers bow, others hesitating.

dialogue.text: Chinese histories name a man called Arunasva, who seized Kannauj in the confusion. Indian inscriptions, however, fall strangely silent about this moment.

i18n.hi: चीनी इतिहास एक अरुणस्व नाम के आदमी का ज़िक्र करते हैं, जिसने इस अफ़रा-तफ़री में कन्नौज दबोच लिया। भारतीय अभिलेख मगर इस घड़ी पर अजीब चुप हैं।

panels.shot: medium interior shot in the Tang court, side angle, with Wang Xuance before the emperor’s dais
panels.action: In a grand Tang hall, Wang Xuance kneels before the distant figure of the Tang emperor, scroll in hand, palace officials in tall hats watching from the shadows.

dialogue.text: Far to the northeast, in Chang’an, the Tang court read of Harsha’s hospitality in earlier years. They chose an envoy, Wang Xuance, to renew ties with the new ruler of ‘Tianzhu’.

i18n.hi: काफ़ी उत्तर-पूर्व, चांगआन में, तांग दरबार हर्ष की पुरानी मेहमाननवाज़ी पढ़ रहा था। उन्होंने ‘तianzhu’ के नए शासक से संबंध ताज़ा करने को वांग श्वान्से को दूत चुना।

panels.shot: tight medium on Wang Xuance as he bows, profile view, eyes intent
panels.action: Wang Xuance bows deeply, face calm but focused, as a court attendant hands him a rolled edict and a small box bearing the Tang imperial seal.

dialogue.speaker: wang_xuance
dialogue.text: Harsha once welcomed us. Will his successor honour that path—or break it?

i18n.hi: हर्ष ने हमें अपनाया था। क्या उसका उत्तराधिकारी वही राह निभाएगा—या तोड़ देगा?

panels.shot: wide shot of a caravan on the Silk Road, with mountains on the horizon
panels.action: A caravan of riders and pack animals moves along a dusty ridge road, banners fluttering, as Wang Xuance rides near the front, scanning the rugged horizon.

dialogue.text: Leading a small mission, Wang rode west and south. The Tang sources remember him as a seasoned envoy, used to the long roads between China, Tibet, Nepal, and India.

i18n.hi: छोटा सा दल लेकर वांग पश्चिम और दक्षिण को निकला। तांग स्रोत उसे मंजा हुआ दूत कहते हैं, जो चीन, तिब्बत, नेपाल और भारत की लंबी राहों का आदी था।

panels.shot: low-angle view from just outside a city gate, envoy’s party in foreground, gate towers looming
panels.action: At the edge of a fortified city resembling Kannauj, Wang Xuance and his small escort approach on horseback, pausing as gate towers loom above, soldiers watching from the battlements.

dialogue.text: But the Kannauj he approached was not Harsha’s court of generous debate. It was a city held by a new master, wary of foreign envoys bearing Tang seals.

i18n.hi: पर जिस कन्नौज के दर पर वो पहुँचा, वह बहस और दान का हर्ष का दरबार नहीं था। यह नए मालिक का शहर था, जो तांग की मुहर लिए विदेशी दूतों से चौकन्ना था।

panels.shot: sudden dynamic mid-shot as soldiers rush from the gate toward Wang’s party
panels.action: Armoured soldiers rush out from the open gate toward Wang Xuance’s small group, spears leveled, as his horse rears slightly and his attendants turn in alarm.

dialogue.text: The Tang histories say that Arunasva’s forces attacked the mission. The envoy, expecting ceremony, met ambush instead, his small party scattered and seized.

i18n.hi: तांग इतिहास लिखते हैं कि अरुणस्व की सेना ने दूत मंडल पर धावा बोला। समारोह की आस में आया दूत घात में फँसा, और उसका छोटा दल तितर-बितर व क़ैद हो गया।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Wang Xuance’s tense face in twilight, hint of a camp or holding area behind
panels.action: By dim firelight, Wang Xuance’s face is tense, jaw set, hands bound with rope, a guarded camp visible in blurred background.

dialogue.text: The Chinese record remembers capture and insult, a grave affront in diplomatic practice. How long he was held, and how he slipped away, the texts leave unsaid.

i18n.hi: चीनी लेखा-बही में बंदी बनाया जाना और अपमान दर्ज है—राजनय में भारी बेइज़्ज़ती। कितने दिन पकड़ा रहा, कैसे निकल भागा, ये पंक्तियाँ नहीं बतातीं।

panels.shot: dynamic night-time wide of a desperate escape through brush and low hills
panels.action: Under a moonlit sky, Wang Xuance and a few companions scramble down a scrub-covered slope, cloaks dark, glancing back toward faint torches on the ridge above.

dialogue.speaker: wang_xuance
dialogue.text: We live, we ride north—and let others decide justice.

i18n.hi: ज़िंदा हैं, उत्तर की ओर घुड़सवारी करते हैं—न्याय का फ़ैसला औरों पर छोड़ देते हैं।

panels.shot: broad, grueling wide of the Himalaya foothills as a tiny group ascends a high path
panels.action: Tiny figures—Wang Xuance and his men—are seen from afar crossing a narrow path above a deep gorge, snow-tinged peaks and windswept prayer flags in the distance.

dialogue.text: From the Ganga plain they fled north, climbing into the Himalayan passes. The Xin Tangshu speaks of a hard return, carrying news of the attack to allies beyond the mountains.

i18n.hi: गंगा के मैदानी इलाक़े से वे उत्तर भागे, हिमालयी दर्रों में चढ़ते हुए। शिन तांगशु कठिन वापसी का ज़िक्र करता है, जब वे पहाड़ों पार के साथियों को हमले की ख़बर ले गए।

panels.shot: interior medium shot in a Nepalese court, Wang addressing a local ruler
panels.action: In a timbered hall decorated with local carvings, Wang Xuance stands before a Nepalese ruler seated cross-legged, courtiers watching as he gestures respectfully toward the south.

dialogue.text: According to the Tang histories, Wang turned first to Nepal, requesting troops. The details are sparse, but they credit the kingdom with lending him horsemen and foot soldiers.

i18n.hi: तांग इतिहास के अनुसार, वांग पहले नेपाल पहुँचा, और सैनिकों की दरख़्वास्त की। विवरण कम हैं, पर वे इस राज्य को उसे सवारों और पैदल सिपाहियों की मदद देने का श्रेय देते हैं।

panels.shot: council-tent medium shot with Tibetan leaders and Wang around a low table
panels.action: Inside a large felt tent, rugged Tibetan chiefs sit around a low table, while Wang Xuance points to a rough map of the plains, the air thick with smoke and tension.

dialogue.text: He then sought aid from Tibet, whose power was rising along the Himalayan rim. Tang texts say Tibetans also supplied men, binding this campaign into the wider politics of the plateau.

i18n.hi: फिर उसने तिब्बत से सहारा माँगा, जिसकी ताक़त हिमालय की कगार पर उभर रही थी। तांग लिखते हैं कि तिब्बतियों ने भी सैनिक भेजे, इस मुहिम को पठार की बड़ी सियासत से बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: epic wide shot of a combined army descending from the hills toward the plains
panels.action: A long line of mounted and marching troops—distinct Nepalese and Tibetan contingents—snakes down a hillside, Wang Xuance riding ahead, pointing toward the hazy plains below.

dialogue.text: With this borrowed army, Wang turned south again. The Tang histories speak of tens of thousands, but modern scholars warn that these numbers may be magnified by pride and distance.

i18n.hi: इस उधारी फ़ौज के साथ वांग फिर दक्षिण मुड़ा। तांग किताबें लाखों की गिनती लिखती हैं, पर आधुनिक विद्वान मानते हैं कि ये आँकड़े शान और दूरी से फूले हुए हैं।

panels.shot: high-angle wide of opposing forces arrayed near a river plain, with Kannauj far in the background
panels.action: On a flat plain near a winding river, two forces line up at a distance, Wang Xuance’s mixed army on one side and Arunasva’s troops on the other, Kannauj’s outline faint on the horizon.

dialogue.text: Somewhere in the central Ganga plain, around 648 or 649, they met Arunasva in battle. The Chinese record is firm on victory, though silent on terrain and Indian viewpoints.

i18n.hi: कहीं मध्य गंगा के मैदान में, लगभग 648 या 649 में, वे अरुणस्व से जंग में भिड़े। चीनी रिकार्ड जीत पर अडिग हैं, पर ज़मीन और भारतीय नज़रियों पर खामोश।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide of the clash at its peak, without gore, emphasizing movement and dust
panels.action: Dust billows as cavalry from Wang’s side drives forward, infantry lines push, and banners of different colours tilt under the strain, Wang Xuance visible on horseback directing the advance.

dialogue.text: They describe charges, pursuit, and Arunasva’s defeat. No Indian inscription confirms or denies this scene; on this field, the only surviving voice is the Tang historian’s brush.

i18n.hi: वे धावा, पीछा और अरुणस्व की हार लिखते हैं। कोई भारतीय शिलालेख इस दृश्य को न मानता, न नकारता; इस मैदान पर बस तांग इतिहासकार की कलम की आवाज़ बची है।

panels.shot: medium shot showing Arunasva bound and guarded, with Wang Xuance watching from a short distance
panels.action: Near a quiet riverside after the battle, Arunasva stands with his hands bound, guarded by soldiers, while Wang Xuance watches from a short distance, face controlled, unreadable.

dialogue.text: According to Xin Tangshu, Arunasva was captured and later taken toward the Tang realm as a prisoner. Even here, the sources differ on his final fate, and Indian texts are silent.

i18n.hi: शिन तांगशु के मुताबिक अरुणस्व पकड़ा गया और क़ैदी बनाकर तांग सीमा की ओर ले जाया गया। यहीं से स्रोत उसके अंजाम पर अलग हो जाते हैं, और भारतीय ग्रंथ चुप ही रहते हैं।

panels.shot: formal court wide of Wang Xuance presenting a prisoner or symbolic token at a Tang audience
panels.action: Back in a Tang audience hall, Wang Xuance stands before the emperor again, now with either Arunasva present under guard or a symbolic token of victory laid on a stand.

dialogue.text: In the Tang version, the affront was answered. Wang, who had once come as a guest to Harsha’s court, returned as the commander of an allied force and bearer of a defeated usurper.

i18n.hi: तांग की कहानी में तो बेइज़्ज़ती का जवाब मिल गया। वांग, जो कभी हर्ष के दरबार में मेहमान बनकर आया था, लौटते वक़्त मित्र फ़ौज का सेनापति और हारे हुए गद्दार का पेशकार बना।

panels.shot: wide contemplative view of Kannauj’s skyline in soft light, with subtle signs of decline
panels.action: Kannauj’s walls and temples rise against a hazy sky, but some structures appear weathered, markets thinly crowded, the river carrying away drifting debris.

dialogue.text: Yet Harsha’s old order did not return. The power vacuum remained, rival kings circled, and Kannauj’s story moved on into new hands, while Chinese pages claimed this brief victory as their own.

i18n.hi: फिर भी हर्ष का पुराना विधान वापस न आया। सत्ता का शून्य बना रहा, प्रतिद्वंद्वी राजा मंडराते रहे, और कन्नौज की कहानी नई हथेलियों में चली गई—जबकि चीनी पन्नों ने इस छोटी जीत को अपना कहकर लिख डाला।

panels.shot: quiet medium close-up of Wang Xuance older, in travel clothes, overlooking a distant landscape
panels.action: An older Wang Xuance stands in simple travel robes on a hill, looking out over a valley road lined with small caravans, the wind catching the edge of his cloak.

dialogue.text: Today, Wang Xuance’s campaign stands as a rare Chinese window on India’s succession crisis after Harsha—a reminder that when a throne falls empty, outsiders’ stories can shape how its fall is remembered.

i18n.hi: आज वांग श्वान्से की यह मुहिम, हर्ष के बाद भारत के उत्तराधिकार संकट पर चीन की एक दुर्लभ खिड़की है—याद दिलाती है कि जब सिंहासन खाली गिरता है, तो बाहरी क़िस्से ही उसकी गिरावट की याद तय कर सकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Tang Envoy Rode the Storm After Harsha’s Fall
subtitle_i18n.hi: तांग दूत ने हर्ष के बाद के तूफ़ान पर कैसे सवारी की
